title: NPS: Your Path to a Tax-Efficient Retirement in India
description: The National Pension System (NPS) is a government-regulated, long-term retirement savings scheme for Indian citizens. It offers significant tax benefits under.

faq.q: Who is eligible to open an NPS account?
faq.a: Any Indian citizen, resident or Non-Resident Indian (NRI), between 18 and 70 years of age can open an NPS account.

faq.q: What is the difference between Tier I and Tier II NPS accounts?
faq.a: Tier I is the primary, tax-benefited retirement account with a lock-in until age 60, while Tier II is a voluntary savings account with no lock-in and generally no tax benefits (except for government employees with a 3-year lock-in).
Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are eligible to open an NPS account. Contributions can be made from NRE/NRO accounts.

faq.q: What happens to my NPS account if I change jobs?
faq.a: Your NPS account (PRAN) is portable across jobs and locations. It remains the same, ensuring continuity in your retirement savings regardless of employment changes.

faq.q: Is NPS entirely tax-free at maturity?
faq.a: At maturity (age 60), 60% of your NPS corpus can be withdrawn as a lump sum, which is entirely tax-free. The remaining 40% must be used to purchase an annuity, and the pension income received from this annuity is taxable as per your income tax slab.

faq.q: How do I choose a Pension Fund Manager (PFM)?
faq.a: You can choose a PFM based on their past performance, investment strategies, and charges. You also have the option to change your PFM once a year.

faq.q: Can I exit NPS before retirement?
faq.a: You can exit NPS before age 60 only after 5 years of contribution. In such a case, 80% of the corpus must be used to purchase an annuity, and only 20% can be withdrawn as a lump sum, which is taxable.
